lesson.title: Facial-recognition databases
lesson.summary: Identify untargeted scraping used to create or expand facial-recognition databases.

prerequisites.reason: The database purpose concerns facial recognition for identity rather than any image archive.
The collection feature is introduced as one element of the database prohibition.

blocks: **Untargeted scraping** in this point concerns collecting facial images from the internet or CCTV footage without a targeted selection as part of the stated database practice.
Identify the source, selection and purpose. Data being publicly visible does not itself remove the prohibition; the point specifically names internet and CCTV sources.

The **facial-database ban** concerns AI systems creating or expanding facial-recognition databases through that untargeted scraping. Read creation/expansion, face images, source and untargeted collection together.

The point specifies placing on the market, putting into service for this purpose, or use. Do not turn it into an unsupported statement that every photo database or every face-related function is identical.

Fictional Northbridge case: a supplier uses AI to gather facial images indiscriminately from internet pages to expand a recognition database. Those stipulated facts fit the conduct the point addresses.

Changed case: a consented identity-enrolment process supplies specific records without such scraping. The facts of this point differ; other biometric, privacy and lawful-basis questions still need assessment.
Record collection sources, targeting, recognition-database role and regulated action. Do not accept 'public data' or a disclosure label as a universal exception.
A result that the untargeted-scraping elements are not established does not establish lawful collection under every other law. The legal conclusion should remain tied to this point.
